_comment: TinkerRocket design tokens — single source of truth for both apps. iOS is the design reference (decision 2026-07-30): the palette is Apple's system-color values, which is what the iOS app has always rendered; Android renders these exact hex values instead of Material defaults. Edit THIS file, then run tools/gen_design_tokens.py and commit the regenerated DesignTokens.swift / DesignTokens.kt (CI checks freshness). Platform-native things stay out of tokens by design: navigation mechanics, touch feedback, fonts (SF Pro cannot ship on Android; sizes/weights align via components).

roles._comment: Semantic color roles → palette entries. One role per user-facing meaning, so a screen never reaches for a raw palette color.

surfaces._comment: iOS system surfaces the app actually uses: cards are systemGray6, row chips inside cards are systemGray5, screens are systemBackground.

shape._comment: dp/pt. radiusButton is THE TinkerRocket radius (56 of 76 cornerRadius calls in the iOS app); radiusChip is the small one (flag chips, mini rows).

spacing._comment: dp/pt, from the iOS screens: .padding() = 16, top-screen VStack spacing = 20, in-row spacing = 12.
